entries.topicDescription: Scheduling deferrable, guaranteed background work with WorkManager.

tips.title: WorkManager guarantees execution even across app restarts and device reboots
tips.content:
A coroutine launched in an Activity or Service-scoped CoroutineScope is
lost the moment its owning component is destroyed or the process is
killed — fine for work that only matters while the app is actively
running, but not for work that must eventually complete no matter what.

WorkManager persists enqueued work requests to disk, and the system
re-schedules and re-runs them even after a process death, or a full device
reboot (after a user force-stop, work resumes the next time the app is launched) — making it the right tool for guaranteed-eventually
work like syncing pending uploads.
tips.codeSnippet:
val uploadRequest = OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder<UploadWorker>()
    .setConstraints(Constraints.Builder().setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.CONNECTED).build())
    .build()

WorkManager.getInstance(context).enqueue(uploadRequest) // survives process death and reboots

tips.title: Add constraints and a backoff policy to make work well-behaved
tips.content:
Constraints tell WorkManager when work is allowed to run: a network type, charging, idle, or sufficient battery and storage. The work waits until they are satisfied, so you don't write code to check.

When a Worker returns Result.retry(), WorkManager reschedules it using the backoff policy. Choose EXPONENTIAL for network calls so a struggling server isn't hammered, and note the minimum backoff is 10 seconds.

tips.title: Chain workers and pass data from one to the next
tips.content:
Work that has steps (download, process, upload) can be expressed as a chain: beginWith runs the first request, then() runs the next only after the previous one succeeds, and a failure stops the chain. Each worker returns output Data, which becomes the next worker's input.

You can also start a chain with several requests in parallel; when they all finish, their outputs are merged for the next step by an InputMerger.

tips.title: Periodic work has a 15-minute minimum and is never exact
tips.content:
PeriodicWorkRequest repeats work at an interval, but the minimum interval is 15 minutes, and shorter values are raised to it. The system runs the work at some point within each period (constraints and Doze can delay it), so don't rely on it for exact timing; use an alarm for that.

Enqueue periodic work as unique work with ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP so that calling your setup code again on every app start doesn't create duplicates or reset the schedule.
tips.codeSnippet:
val request = PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<SyncWorker>(1, TimeUnit.HOURS)
    .setConstraints(Constraints.Builder().setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.CONNECTED).build())
    .build()

WorkManager.getInstance(context).enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(
    "sync",
    ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP,   // already scheduled: leave it alone
    request
)

tips.title: Run urgent work as expedited work
tips.content:
Expedited work is for short, important tasks that should start right away even when the app is in the background, such as finishing something the user just triggered. Mark the request with setExpedited and choose what happens when the app's expedited quota is used up: run as regular work or drop the request.

On devices older than Android 12, expedited work is run as a foreground service, so your CoroutineWorker must implement getForegroundInfo to supply the notification it will show.
